_meta.description: Machine-readable action spec for the my_env2 chat environment. Consumed by the symbolic sequence generator (which reads only `produces`/`consumes`/`preconditions`), by the authoring stages (which read every `description`, `returns` and `reference_modes` entry), and by replay (which reads `params`).
_meta.source_of_truth: my_env2/servers/tool.py (local chat tools) and my_env2/servers/web.py (remote DeepWiki tools). Keep this file in sync when tools change.

actor.description: The acting user's id. Every write is attributed to this user; reads are scoped to it where noted.

precondition_semantics.enforced: The tool itself checks it and returns an {"error": ...} object if violated (the action does not take effect).
precondition_semantics.soft: Not checked by the tool, but required for the action to be meaningful/verifiable; the generator must satisfy it when seeding.

reference_mode_semantics.purpose: A reference mode is a way of picking an entity out of the environment by describing it rather than by naming its id. The authoring pass assigns one mode per core entity; the prompt then refers to that entity through the mode's `phrase` instead of its id, so an agent has to inspect the environment to resolve it.
reference_mode_semantics.contract: Each mode is a Boolean predicate over environment state, parameterised by `params`. The adapter must implement it as `resolve(state, mode, params) -> [entity_id]`, returning every entity that satisfies it; a mode is usable for a given entity only when that list is exactly [entity]. Every mode is GLOBALLY scoped: it names no other entity, so uniqueness is decidable without resolving a second reference and `phrase` needs no nesting.
reference_mode_semantics.readability: `readable_via` lists the actions an agent needs, in combination, to observe the property during a rollout — enumerating the candidates as well as reading the property off them. A mode no set of tools can observe would make the task unsolvable rather than hard, so this field is load-bearing, not documentation.
reference_mode_semantics.ordering: Modes are declared most indirect first. That order is the fallback the pipeline walks when the authoring pass proposes nothing usable, so a reference that has to be derived still asks the agent to work something out rather than restating a name.

user.description: A person in the workspace. Display names may collide; handles never do.

params.name: text
params.description: a distinctive phrase appearing in exactly one message, which that user wrote

reference_modes.predicate: the user who wrote the one message whose text contains {text}
the user who has written more messages than any other across the workspace (strictly more, so there is no tie)
reference_modes.phrase: the person who has posted the most across all your chats

reference_modes.predicate: the user whose display name is exactly {name}, and who is the only such user

params.name: handle
params.description: the user's exact handle, without a leading @

reference_modes.predicate: the user whose handle is exactly {handle}

chat.description: A conversation the acting user takes part in. `name` is null for a DM.

params.name: text
params.description: a distinctive phrase appearing in exactly one chat

reference_modes.predicate: the chat containing a message whose text contains {text}
the only chat holding at least one message the acting user has not read
reference_modes.phrase: the one conversation you still have not caught up on

params.name: count
params.description: how many members the chat has, counting the acting user

reference_modes.predicate: the chat that has exactly {count} members, and is the only chat with that many
reference_modes.phrase: the conversation with exactly {count} people in it

reference_modes.predicate: the chat whose title is exactly {name}

message.description: One posted message. `reply_to` threads it under an earlier message in the same chat.

params.name: text
params.description: a distinctive phrase in the PARENT message, which must have exactly one reply

reference_modes.predicate: the single reply to the one message whose text contains {text}
reference_modes.phrase: the reply to the message about {text}

reference_modes.predicate: the message with strictly more distinct reactors than any other in the workspace
reference_modes.phrase: the message that has drawn the most reactions

params.name: handle
params.description: the author's exact handle, without a leading @

reference_modes.predicate: the most recent message written by the user whose handle is {handle}

params.name: text
params.description: a distinctive phrase appearing in exactly one message

reference_modes.predicate: the one message whose text contains {text}

chat.state: per-rollout ChatState, synced through the rollout state channel
chat.description: Local mock chat app. Read and write tools operate on the rollout's ChatState.

deepwiki.description: Public DeepWiki MCP server: read-only GitHub-repo Q&A. Answers can be nondeterministic; requires the repo to be indexed by DeepWiki.

actions.description: List the chats the acting user is a member of.
actions.returns: array of {id, kind, name, members} for chats where actor is in member_ids

actions.description: Read the most recent messages in a chat, oldest to newest.

preconditions.description: If the chat does not exist the tool returns an empty list (no error); a valid read targets an existing chat.

meaningful_when.requirement: the chat already has messages in it. A chat created during this task holds nothing worth reading, so reading it returns no information a later step could carry.

actions.returns: array of message views {id, chat_id, from, sender_id, text, ts, reply_to, reactions, read_by}

actions.description: Look up a user by id.

preconditions.description: If the user does not exist the tool returns {"error": "no such user"}.

actions.description: Send a message from the acting user to a chat.

preconditions.description: The destination chat must exist; otherwise the tool returns {"error": "no such chat"} and nothing is written.

effect.summary: appends a new message from the actor to the chat

mutations.description: new Message(id=m_<next>, chat_id, sender_id=actor, text, ts=max(ts)+1, reply_to=null, read_by=[actor])

actions.description: Reply to an existing message in its chat (threaded).

preconditions.description: The parent message must exist; otherwise the tool returns {"error": "no such message"} and nothing is written.

effect.summary: appends a new message that references the parent, in the parent's chat

mutations.description: new Message(chat_id=parent.chat_id, sender_id=actor, text, ts=max(ts)+1, reply_to=message_id, read_by=[actor])

actions.description: Add an emoji reaction from the acting user to a message.

preconditions.description: The target message must exist; otherwise the tool returns {"error": "no such message"}.

effect.summary: adds the actor to the message's reaction set for the emoji (idempotent)

mutations.description: actor id appended if not already present

meaningful_when.requirement: the acting user has not already reacted to this message, and no other step of the task reacts to it — a second reaction writes a fact that is already true and so is worth nothing.

actions.description: Mark every message in a chat as read by the acting user.

preconditions.description: Not checked; a nonexistent or empty chat simply marks 0 messages. A meaningful mark_read targets a chat with unread messages.

effect.summary: adds the actor to read_by of each not-yet-read message in the chat

mutations.target: state.messages[*].read_by (where chat_id matches and actor absent)
mutations.description: actor appended to read_by of each qualifying message

meaningful_when.requirement: the chat holds at least one message the acting user has not read — on a fully-read or empty chat this action changes nothing.

actions.description: Create a new chat; the acting user is always included as a member.

params.name: member_ids
params.description: user ids to include (actor added automatically)

params.name: name
params.description: chat name; if set (or >2 members) the chat is a group, else a dm

preconditions.description: Not checked, but member_ids should reference existing users for the chat to be meaningful/verifiable.

effect.summary: adds a new chat containing the actor and the given members

mutations.description: new Chat(id=c_<next_chat_id>, kind=group if name or >2 members else dm, name, member_ids=[actor, *member_ids] deduped)

actions.description: Ask an AI-grounded question about a GitHub repository.

params.name: repoName
params.description: GitHub repo in owner/repo form (or a list, max 10)

preconditions.description: The repo must be indexed by DeepWiki. Answers are LLM-generated and may vary run-to-run; prefer questions with stable, unambiguous answers.

actions.returns: a free-text answer to any question about the repo — metadata (licence, primary language, maintainers) and prose questions alike. Nondeterministic wording, so only ask things with a stable, unambiguous answer.

actions.description: View DeepWiki documentation for a GitHub repository.

preconditions.description: The repo must be indexed by DeepWiki. Content can drift as the repo/docs change (no version pinning).

actions.returns: the repo's wiki DOCUMENTATION PROSE. It states what the project is for, how a subsystem works, what a concept means. It does NOT state licence, stars, maintainers or primary language, so a question about those has no obtainable answer here.

actions.description: List the DeepWiki documentation topics for a GitHub repository.

preconditions.description: The repo must be indexed by DeepWiki.

actions.returns: only the LIST OF DOCUMENTATION TOPIC TITLES. It can answer which areas the documentation covers, and nothing about repo metadata or the content of any page.
